## **2\. Product Background** {#2.-product-background}

Education technology is shifting from one-way content delivery toward creator-led learning ecosystems, where instructors self-publish their learning products and learners expect personalized guidance, interactivity, and measurable progress. Japanese language learning remains a significantly sized niche market in Vietnam. The Japan Foundation recorded 169,582 Japanese language learners in Vietnam in its 2021 survey, and the 2024 update still ranks Vietnam sixth globally with 164,495 learners. This indicates that the demand is large enough to justify developing a specialized digital product for Japanese language learning. 

![][image2]

However, the current market is fragmented. Learners can purchase video-on-demand (VOD) courses from generic course platforms, practice vocabulary via mobile apps, join social media groups, or pay for in-person classes. Each option only solves a fraction of the learning journey. As a result, students often lack a unified learning environment that integrates course content, practical activities, instructor-created modules, AI support, progress tracking, and course ownership.

* **For learners:** Traditional VOD courses can become passive and tedious because they often rely on long recorded videos. When facing difficulties with vocabulary, grammar, Kanji, or sentence structure in a specific lesson, they are often isolated and have to wait for an instructor's response, search external sources themselves, or abandon the lesson. This diminishes discipline and increases the risk of dropping out during self-study.  
* **For teachers:** Many independent Japanese instructors possess solid expertise but lack the technical infrastructure to self-publish, sell, and operate online courses. Existing learning management systems (LMS) are often expensive, complex, or not optimized for Japanese content. Teachers also need a workflow that supports student writing practice without incorrectly positioning AI as a replacement for human academic judgment. In ManabiHub, teachers remain responsible for official feedback and scoring when a course requires formal writing evaluation, while AI is used only to provide preliminary learning suggestions for students.

To better understand these challenges, the project team conducted a practical survey involving center managers, teachers, and students directly participating in Japanese teaching and learning. The survey results revealed a massive demand for personalized learning support tools, progress tracking systems, Kanji revision tools, and extracurricular learning solutions. Furthermore, the survey demonstrated a high level of user readiness to adopt and utilize Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies in an educational environment. These findings indicate a clear opportunity to develop a specialized platform capable of simultaneously addressing learning and management issues within the same ecosystem.

![][image3]

ManabiHub is proposed as a specialized e-learning marketplace for Japanese language education. This platform acts as an intermediary between students and teachers, allowing teachers to create and sell structured Japanese courses, while students learn through interactive modules and AI assistance. The commercial model is a revenue-sharing platform: teachers receive the majority of the course revenue, while the platform collects a commission from each successful transaction.

The platform's commission is used to maintain server infrastructure, operate payment and marketplace functions, and fund the AI ecosystem. To protect unit economics, ManabiHub combines basic free access (freemium) with a flexible AI quota model:

* To protect platform unit economics, ManabiHub does not provide unlimited AI usage for every course. AI Chatbot and AI Writing Assistance are enabled only for enrolled Students in courses that meet or exceed the configured AI support price floor. Free courses or courses priced below the AI support price floor still provide normal learning content, quizzes, flashcards, writing practice, and progress tracking, but do not provide AI Chatbot or AI Writing Assistance. AI Writing Assistance provides preliminary suggestions for grammar, vocabulary, sentence structure, and revision guidance. These suggestions are clearly treated as non-official learning support and must not be used as final grading.  
* This approach allows the platform to control AI operating cost through course pricing and system configuration instead of selling separate AI token packages in the MVP. AI usage is still logged for monitoring, abuse prevention, and future optimization, but Students do not manage a separate AI token wallet.

The primary goal of ManabiHub is to enhance learning efficiency, increase student engagement, and reduce repetitive course operation work for independent instructors without replacing the pedagogical role of teachers. The system targets two core user groups: learners seeking a flexible, interactive, and AI-supported educational experience; and teachers requiring an optimized technical infrastructure to self-publish, operate, and monetize their courses. By focusing on a lean marketplace model combined with a content seeding strategy during the MVP phase, the project ensures technical feasibility and effective platform cost control before scaling up. In the long term, ManabiHub aims to become a leading creator-led smart learning ecosystem, elevating the quality of Japanese language education through responsible AI-supported learning tools and delivering sustainable economic value to the teaching community. 

## **3\. Existing Systems** {#3.-existing-systems}

### **3.1 Udemy**  {#3.1-udemy}

**Website:** [https://www.udemy.com/](https://www.udemy.com/)

Udemy is a global online learning marketplace that allows individual instructors, educational organizations, and training providers to publish and sell online courses to learners. In this model, Udemy functions as an intermediary platform that connects course creators with end users. Learners can search for courses, view course descriptions, check ratings and reviews, make payments, and access learning materials online.

In the field of Japanese language learning, Udemy provides a wide range of courses, including beginner Japanese, JLPT preparation, Japanese grammar, Kanji, vocabulary, listening practice, and conversational Japanese. This makes Udemy relevant to the B2B2C model because instructors or educational organizations act as the business providers, Udemy acts as the platform provider, and learners are the final customers.

From a B2B2C perspective, Udemy has several advantages. First, it provides an established marketplace structure where instructors can upload course content and reach a large number of learners. Second, the platform supports course purchasing, video-based learning, course ratings, reviews, certificates, and lifetime access to purchased courses. Third, Udemy reduces the technical burden for instructors because they do not need to build their own learning management system.

However, Udemy is a general-purpose learning platform rather than a platform specifically designed for Japanese language education. Therefore, it does not fully support specialized Japanese learning features such as Hiragana and Katakana writing practice, Kanji stroke-order practice, JLPT-style exercises, vocabulary flashcards, spaced repetition, grammar drills by JLPT level, or detailed language-learning progress tracking. In addition, although learners can watch course videos, the platform may not provide enough interactive practice after each lesson. As a result, Udemy is strong in online course selling but less specialized in Japanese language learning and practice.

**Relevant source:** Udemy describes itself as a platform for learning online courses, and its instructor resources show that instructors can create and publish courses on the platform.

### **3.2 Coto Academy Online**  {#3.2-coto-academy-online}

**Website:** [https://cotoacademy.com/online-japanese-class/](https://cotoacademy.com/online-japanese-class/)

Coto Academy Online is an online Japanese language learning platform operated by Coto Japanese Academy. It provides online Japanese lessons for learners who want to study with professional Japanese teachers. The system allows learners to create an account, choose suitable courses, purchase lesson points, book classes, and manage their study schedule online.

Coto Academy Online can be considered close to a B2B2C model because the academy and its teachers provide educational services through an online platform, while learners are the final users of those services. Unlike a fully open marketplace such as Udemy, Coto Academy is more centralized because the courses and teachers mainly belong to the academy itself. However, the platform still shows how a Japanese learning service can combine online course management, teacher-led learning, scheduling, and learner access in one system.

One important strength of Coto Academy Online is its focus on real-time teacher interaction. Learners can join group lessons or private lessons, which makes the system suitable for learners who want to improve speaking, communication skills, and practical Japanese usage. The platform also provides many course options, allowing learners to choose classes based on their learning goals and proficiency level. According to Coto Academy, students can buy lesson points, book classes, and manage their schedule in one place.

However, Coto Academy Online mainly focuses on teacher-led classes and lesson booking. This means that it may not be as strong in automated self-study functions such as flashcards, Kanji drills, grammar quizzes, JLPT mock tests, vocabulary review systems, or self-paced video learning. For learners who want to practice independently after lessons, the platform may still require additional learning tools. Therefore, Coto Academy Online is strong in live Japanese instruction but less focused on automated practice and course marketplace functions.

### **3.3 SNG Online Japanese Language School**  {#3.3-sng-online-japanese-language-school}

 Website: [https://www.sng.ac.jp/en/online-japanese-class/](https://www.sng.ac.jp/en/online-japanese-class/)

SNG Online Japanese Language School is an online Japanese language education service operated by Shinjuku Japanese Language Institute. It provides Japanese courses for different learning levels, including beginner, intermediate, business Japanese, and JLPT preparation courses. The school emphasizes instruction by native and certified Japanese teachers based in Tokyo.

In terms of system model, SNG Online Japanese Language School is closer to an online school model than a fully open marketplace. The institution itself provides the courses, teachers, and learning programs, while learners register and study through its online system. Therefore, it has some B2B2C characteristics because an educational organization uses an online platform to deliver Japanese language education to learners. However, it is not a marketplace where multiple independent centers or instructors can freely publish and sell their own courses.

A major strength of SNG is its structured academic approach. The platform offers courses for different purposes, such as foundational Japanese, intermediate Japanese, business Japanese, and JLPT preparation. Its JLPT course includes important components such as vocabulary, Kanji, grammar, reading, and listening comprehension. This makes the system suitable for learners who want a more formal and guided Japanese learning experience.

Nevertheless, SNG also has several limitations when compared with an open B2B2C Japanese learning platform. First, the system is mainly managed by one educational institution, so it does not support multiple independent course providers in the same way as a marketplace. Second, learners may have fewer choices of instructors and course styles compared with an open platform. Third, although SNG provides structured online classes, it may not offer flexible marketplace features such as public course reviews, multi-provider course comparison, instructor dashboards, or course-selling tools for external Japanese centers. In addition, automated learning tools such as flashcards, gamified quizzes, Kanji practice, and personalized progress tracking may not be as flexible as those in a dedicated learning-practice platform.

### 

### **3.4 Nihongo Master**  {#3.4-nihongo-master}

### 

Website: [https://www.nihongomaster.com/](https://www.nihongomaster.com/)

Nihongo Master is an online Japanese learning platform that provides structured lessons, quizzes, drills, a Japanese dictionary, a Kanji dictionary, handwriting practice, and a learner community. The platform is designed specifically for Japanese language learners and offers content aligned with JLPT levels, especially from beginner level to JLPT N3. According to Nihongo Master, the system includes lessons, spaced repetition drills, quizzes, dictionaries, handwriting practice, and community features in one place.

From a system perspective, Nihongo Master is different from general online course marketplaces such as Udemy. Instead of mainly allowing external instructors to upload and sell courses, Nihongo Master focuses on providing its own structured Japanese learning path. Learners can study at their own pace, review vocabulary and grammar through drills, use dictionaries, complete quizzes, and track their learning progress through the platform.

One of the main strengths of Nihongo Master is that it is specifically designed for Japanese language learning. It supports important learning components such as Hiragana, Katakana, vocabulary, Kanji, grammar, quizzes, and spaced repetition review. These features are useful for helping learners memorize Japanese characters, review vocabulary regularly, and reinforce grammar knowledge. In addition, the platform also provides handwriting practice, which is important because writing Kana and Kanji can help learners remember Japanese characters more effectively.

However, Nihongo Master is closer to a B2C learning platform than a full B2B2C marketplace. The platform mainly provides learning content directly to learners, rather than allowing many independent Japanese language centers or instructors to publish and sell their own courses. Therefore, although Nihongo Master is strong in Japanese learning and self-practice features, it may not fully support marketplace functions such as multi-provider course management, instructor dashboards, course approval workflows, revenue sharing, course reviews for different providers, or center-based learner management.

For the proposed system, Nihongo Master is a useful reference for designing the learning and practice features. Its strengths show the importance of integrating structured lessons, quizzes, flashcards or spaced repetition, Kanji learning, dictionaries, and progress tracking. However, the proposed system aims to go further by combining these Japanese-specific practice features with a B2B2C course-selling model, where Japanese language centers or instructors can publish and manage their own courses.

### **3.5 JF Japanese e-Learning Minato**   {#3.5-jf-japanese-e-learning-minato}

**Website:** [https://minato-jf.jp/](https://minato-jf.jp/)

JF Japanese e-Learning Minato is an online Japanese language learning platform provided by the Japan Foundation. The platform describes itself as “a place to learn and meet,” where users can study Japanese, learn about Japanese culture, and connect with other learners who share similar interests. The Japan Foundation also states that Minato allows users to take online Japanese courses and interact with worldwide communities of learners.

Minato provides online Japanese courses for learners around the world, especially those who may not be able to attend Japanese language classes because of geographical, time, or financial limitations. The Japan Foundation explains that Minato was developed to provide learning opportunities for people who cannot attend regular Japanese classes and for those who want to start learning Japanese online.

From a system perspective, Minato is a structured e-learning platform rather than a commercial course marketplace. Learners can register for an account, browse available courses, enroll in online courses, and study Japanese through the platform. Some courses are self-study based, while others may include tutor support or community interaction. The platform also includes cultural learning elements, which makes it different from systems that only focus on grammar, vocabulary, or exam preparation.

A major strength of Minato is its credibility and educational quality because it is provided by the Japan Foundation, an official organization that promotes Japanese language and culture internationally. The platform is suitable for learners who want structured, reliable, and culturally connected Japanese learning content. It also supports a global learning community, allowing users to learn not only the language but also aspects of Japanese society and culture.

However, Minato is not primarily designed as a B2B2C marketplace for course selling. It does not mainly focus on allowing many independent Japanese centers, instructors, or training organizations to upload, sell, and manage their own courses. In addition, because it is more education-oriented and institution-based, its commercial functions such as course pricing, online payment, provider revenue management, course marketing, learner reviews, and multi-center administration may be limited compared with a marketplace platform.

For the proposed system, Minato is a useful reference for structured Japanese learning and cultural integration. It demonstrates the importance of providing organized learning content, online course enrollment, and a community-based learning environment. However, the proposed system will focus more strongly on combining online course business functions with Japanese-specific learning tools. This means that the proposed platform will support not only learners but also Japanese language centers and instructors who need tools to publish courses, manage students, sell learning content, and track learner performance.

| System | Model | Main Strengths | Main Limitations |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| Udemy | Open course marketplace | Course selling, video learning, reviews, large user base | Not specialized for Japanese learning |
| Coto Academy Online | Online Japanese school platform | Live lessons, booking system, teacher interaction | Less focused on automated self-practice |
| SNG Online Japanese Language School | Online Japanese school | Structured courses, JLPT and business Japanese | Not an open marketplace for many providers |
| Nihongo Master | Japanese self-learning platform | JLPT-based lessons, quizzes, SRS drills, Kanji and dictionary tools | Not a B2B2C marketplace for multiple course providers |
| JF Japanese e-Learning Minato | Institutional e-learning platform | Reliable content, online courses, cultural learning, global community | Limited commercial marketplace and multi-provider functions |

## **4\. Business Opportunity** {#4.-business-opportunity}

The business opportunity for ManabiHub comes from the gap between strong demand for Japanese learning and the lack of a dedicated digital marketplace that combines teacher monetization, interactive Japanese pedagogy, and AI support. Vietnam remains one of the largest countries for Japanese-language learners according to Japan Foundation survey results, while the global Japanese-language learner base reached about 4 million in the 2024 survey. \[1\]  
The commercial environment is attractive because three groups have aligned incentives. Students want more effective online learning and timely support. Teachers want a low-barrier way to publish, sell, and scale their courses. The platform needs recurring commission revenue and controlled AI operating costs to maintain infrastructure and improve learning-support services. A specialized marketplace can create value for all three groups by reducing transaction friction and increasing learning completion quality.  
Existing platforms prove that individual parts of the opportunity are viable: Udemy validates marketplace-based instructor monetization, Duolingo validates gamification and freemium language learning, MochiMochi validates habit-based vocabulary review for Vietnamese learners, and Minato validates Japanese-specific online course demand. However, none of these systems fully combines all required capabilities for a Vietnam-focused Japanese course marketplace with AI support, teacher revenue settlement, refund governance, and lesson-contextual interaction.  
ManabiHub is attractive because it targets a focused niche instead of competing as a generic LMS. The product can start with a small MVP containing seed JLPT courses, course purchase, lesson modules, AI chatbot, AI Writing Assistance, teacher official feedback when required, and basic wallet settlement. After proof of concept, the marketplace can onboard external teachers, expand levels from N5 to N1, and introduce more advanced features such as teacher analytics, advanced AI learning support, community discussions, and recommendation algorithms.

## **5\. Software Product Vision** {#5.-software-product-vision}

For Vietnamese learners who want to study Japanese online with structured guidance and timely support, ManabiHub is a specialized e-learning marketplace that allows learners to purchase teacher-created Japanese courses, study through interactive lesson modules, ask a context-aware AI chatbot for help, and use AI Writing Assistance for preliminary revision suggestions. Unlike generic VOD platforms and standalone vocabulary apps, ManabiHub combines Japanese-specific pedagogy, instructor monetization, responsible AI-supported learning, course ownership protection, and controlled marketplace cash flow in one platform.  
When ManabiHub is successfully deployed, Japanese learners will no longer need to jump between video platforms, flashcard apps, social groups, and disconnected learning tools. Teachers will be able to launch digital courses without building their own LMS or payment system, while still retaining responsibility for official academic feedback when required. The platform will become a trusted marketplace where learners progress more consistently, teachers scale their expertise, and internal staff can govern course quality, refunds, role-based permissions, and revenue settlement transparently.

## **6\. Project Scope & Limitations** {#6.-project-scope-&-limitations}

### **6.1 Major Features** {#6.1-major-features}

The following features define the core functions included in the MVP scope of ManabiHub :

* **FE-01**: Public Google OAuth access, first-time Student/Teacher role onboarding, profile management, and role-based access control.  
* **FE-02**: Teacher KYC submission and digital copyright agreement before course publication.  
* **FE-03**: Course creation through a Modular Builder with video, text, quiz, flashcard, and writing assignment blocks.  
* **FE-04**: Auto-validation rules for course metadata, title length, course introduction, video duration, and mandatory interaction blocks after long videos.  
* **FE-05**: Course marketplace with search, filter, category, course detail, preview, price, rating, and teacher profile information.  
* **FE-06**: Course purchase and secure payment flow integrated with a payment gateway webhook.  
* **FE-07**: Digital course ownership that keeps paid learners’ access even when a course is hidden or soft-deleted for new buyers.  
* **FE-08**: Student learning player that displays lesson modules, tracks progress, and records completion status.  
* **FE-09:** Context-aware AI chatbot that answers questions using the current lesson text or transcript as context for eligible enrolled courses.

* **FE-10:** AI Writing Assistance that provides preliminary suggestions on grammar, vocabulary, sentence structure, and revision direction for student writing practice in AI-supported courses. AI suggestions are non-official learning support and are not used as final grades.

* **FE-11**: Teacher writing review workflow that allows teachers to review student writing submissions and provide official feedback or scores when a course requires formal writing evaluation. Teacher feedback is stored separately from AI suggestions.  
* **FE-12**: Gamification features including streaks, badges, progress indicators, and automated reminder notifications.  
* **FE-13**: Rating and review functions are limited to verified course owners. Violation reporting is available to logged-in Students and Teachers with anti-spam and moderation controls.   
* **FE-14:** Shared wallet and escrow system with Pending\_Clearing, Available Balance, course payment balance, teacher revenue split, platform commission, and payout tracking.

* **FE-15:** Auto-refund logic based on purchase time within 14 days and learning progress not exceeding 20%, with dispute escalation for non-eligible cases.

* **FE-16:** Admin Portal dashboard with role-based access for System Admin, Course Manager, and Finance Manager. System Admin manages configuration and internal roles; Course Manager handles KYC, course approval, and violation moderation; Finance Manager handles refund, payout, and transaction reconciliation.

* **FE-17:** Final Test and certificate eligibility workflow. A Student receives a course completion certificate only after reaching 100% required progress, completing required assignments, achieving average required exercise score of at least 85%, and passing the course Final Test. 

* **FE-18**: MVP content seeding support for 1-2 internally created JLPT courses used to validate the marketplace and learning flow.  
* **FE-19:** Separate Admin Portal with pre-created internal accounts, password-hash security, audit logging, and restricted administration functions for System Admin, Course Manager, and Finance Manager.

![][image4]

### **6.2 Limitations** {#6.2-limitations}

The following features and characteristics may be expected by stakeholders but are explicitly excluded from the MVP scope:

* **LI-01:** The MVP is web-based. Native iOS and Android mobile applications are excluded from the first release.  
* **LI-02:** The platform will not provide official JLPT certification or official exam scoring. AI Writing Assistance is only a preliminary learning-support feature and must not be treated as official grading. Teacher feedback remains the official source of assessment when a course requires formal writing evaluation.  
* **LI-03:** Live classroom streaming, video conferencing, and real-time group teaching are excluded from the MVP unless added in a future phase  
* **LI-04:** The system will not guarantee unlimited AI usage. AI Chatbot and AI Writing Assistance are available only for enrolled Students in courses whose price is equal to or higher than the configured AI support price floor. Free courses or courses below this threshold do not include AI support in the MVP.  
* **LI-05:** The platform will not automatically produce legal tax invoices or handle full teacher taxation/accounting requirements in the MVP.  
* **LI-06:** International payment gateways and multi-currency settlement are excluded. The initial target is domestic Vietnam-focused payments.  
* **LI-07:** The system cannot completely prevent copyright infringement before publication. It will rely on teacher KYC, digital agreement, reporting, moderation, and post-violation enforcement.  
* **LI-08:** ManabiHub will not guarantee permanent availability of hidden/violating content for new buyers. Soft delete protects only students who purchased before the course was hidden or locked.  
* **LI-09:** AI answers and AI writing suggestions may be inaccurate or incomplete. The platform will display an AI disclaimer and clearly label AI Writing Assistance as non-official preliminary support. AI output must not be used as final academic grading.  
* **LI-10:** The MVP will not include a full social network, open forum, or peer-to-peer messaging system beyond essential course learning and support workflows.  
* **LI-11:** Advanced recommendation engines, adaptive learning paths, proctoring, and plagiarism detection are considered future enhancements, not mandatory MVP functions.  
* **LI-12:** Physical textbooks, printed materials, offline classroom operations, and shipping/logistics are outside the software product scope.  
* **LI-13:** The MVP does not provide separate AI token packages or a standalone AI token wallet for Students. AI cost control is handled through course eligibility, price floor configuration, AI guardrails, and usage logging.
